examples.knowledge_point: Applying De Moivre's Theorem With a Negative Sine
examples.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{4}} & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

For expressions involving subtraction, De Moivre's theorem states that

$$
\left[ \cos (\varphi) - \textrm{i}\sin(\varphi) \right]^n = \cos(n\varphi) - \textrm{i}\sin{(n\varphi)}.
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\varphi=2\theta.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}^{-4} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-4\cdot 2\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-4\cdot 2\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\cos(-\varphi) = \cos (\varphi)$ and $\sin(-\varphi) = -\sin(\varphi)$ for any input $\varphi,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta ) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-[-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )] \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, note that

$$
\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}}=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4}.
$$

De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡\phi +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡\phi ]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=-4$ and $\phi =2\theta .$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{4}} & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]^{-4} \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2(-4)\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2(-4)\theta )] \\  & =2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the fact that $\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\phi )=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\phi )=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )$ for any input $\phi ,$ we have

$$
2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(-8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-8\theta )]=2[\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )-\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta )].
$$
